projects.name: Customer Analytics Dashboard
projects.description:
End-to-end analytics dashboard project covering three data domains: (1) customer data processing from CSV exports, (2) application log analysis, and (3) visualization components. Scope includes ingestion, validation, storage/modeling, metrics/API, UI dashboards, and production launch readiness (testing, security/PII review, docs, monitoring, phased rollout). Structured as 6 milestones with leaf tasks sized for execution in roughly 0.5–3 days each.

Tags: analytics, dashboard, data-pipeline, etl, csv, log-analysis, visualization, greenfield

tasks.name: M1 — Discovery & Foundations
tasks.details: Milestone: establish scope, data source inventory, architecture, and working development environment before any pipeline code is written. Exit criteria: signed-off requirements, documented CSV and log source inventories, agreed architecture decision records, repo + CI green.

tasks.name: M2 — Ingestion & Data Processing
tasks.details: Milestone: build and harden the batch ingestion paths for customer CSV files and application logs, including validation, normalization, deduplication, PII handling, error categorization, and orchestration. Exit criteria: both sources land in storage on a schedule with data-quality gates and quarantine for bad records.

tasks.name: M3 — Storage & Data Modeling
tasks.details: Milestone: model curated and consumption-ready data for both domains — customer dimensions/segments and application-health facts — with partitioning, retention, and cost controls. Exit criteria: versioned transformations, documented schema, and marts that serve the agreed metrics without full-table scans.

tasks.name: M4 — Metrics & Analytics API
tasks.details: Milestone: define the metric catalog once, implement performant aggregations, and expose them through a versioned, authenticated API with caching. Exit criteria: every dashboard metric traces to a documented definition and API p95 latency meets the target under expected load.

tasks.name: M5 — Visualization & Dashboard UI
tasks.details: Milestone: deliver the dashboard experience — shell, customer analytics views, log analysis views, and interactivity (filters, drilldowns, export). Exit criteria: stakeholder-approved UX, all agreed charts implemented against live API data, and accessibility basics verified.

tasks.name: M6 — Quality, Security & Launch
tasks.details: Milestone: prove the platform is correct, fast, secure, and operable, then release it. Exit criteria: test suite green in CI, load test within budget, security/PII sign-off, UAT accepted, runbooks published, monitoring live, phased rollout complete.

tasks.name: 1.1 Requirements & success metrics workshop
tasks.details: Facilitate a 2-hour workshop with stakeholders to capture the top user questions the dashboard must answer, the KPIs per audience (exec, support, customer success), refresh cadence, and explicit success criteria. Output: one-page scope doc + prioritized KPI list. Do not design charts yet.

tasks.name: 1.2 Inventory & profile customer CSV sources
tasks.details: Collect one sample export per CSV source and document: producer system, delivery method (SFTP/email/manual), frequency, volume, encoding, delimiter, header quirks, column meanings, primary key candidates, null rates, and known dirty-data patterns. Output: source inventory sheet + a profiling notebook/script. Keep each source as a row so the work stays mechanical.

tasks.name: 1.3 Inventory & profile application log sources
tasks.details: For each service/environment, document log format (JSON vs plaintext), timestamp format/timezone, severity levels, request IDs/trace IDs, retention, access path (S3, CloudWatch, Splunk, files), and daily volume. Pull a 1000-line sample per service and catalogue field presence. Output: log source inventory + sample corpus for parser tests.

tasks.name: 1.4 Architecture & tech stack decision records
tasks.details: Choose and record decisions for: warehouse/store (e.g. Postgres vs DuckDB vs BigQuery), transformation tool (dbt/SQL), orchestration (cron/Airflow/Dagster), API framework, and frontend charting library. Produce 5 short ADRs (context, options, decision, consequences) plus one architecture diagram. Timebox to avoid analysis paralysis.

tasks.name: 1.5 Repo, dev environment & CI pipeline
tasks.details: Create the monorepo (or repos) with directory skeleton for ingestion/, transforms/, api/, web/, plus README and Makefile. Set up local dev via Docker Compose (database + mock storage), pre-commit linting/formatting, and a CI workflow that runs lint + tests on every PR. Definition of done: a trivial PR goes green end-to-end.

tasks.name: 1.6 Data classification & PII policy draft
tasks.details: Tag every field found in 1.2 and 1.3 as public / internal / PII / sensitive (email, phone, address, IP, user IDs). Decide masking/hashing/tokenization approach and who may query raw vs masked data. Output: one-page policy table the pipeline and API tasks can implement directly. Coordinate with legal/security reviewer.

tasks.name: 2.1 CSV reader & schema contracts
tasks.details: Implement a reusable CSV reader that handles encoding detection (UTF-8/latin-1), delimiter sniffing, quoted fields/newlines, BOM, and header normalization. Encode one explicit schema contract per source (column name, type, required/optional, max length) from the 1.2 inventory. Fail loudly with a readable diff when a file's header drifts.

tasks.name: 2.2 Customer normalization, dedupe & ID resolution
tasks.details: Standardize names/emails/phones/country codes/dates, trim and collapse whitespace, unify booleans and currency. Deduplicate on deterministic keys (email normalized + source), and define survivorship rules for conflicting rows (most recent non-null wins). Emit a stable customer_id mapping table plus a reject list with reasons.

tasks.name: 2.3 PII masking & hashing at ingestion
tasks.details: Implement the 1.6 policy in code: hash emails/phones with a salted, key-managed function for joins while storing masked display values; drop or tokenize free-text fields that may contain PII; redact IPs in logs to /24 or hash. Add unit tests with known inputs and document key rotation. No raw PII in the analytics layer.

tasks.name: 2.4 Structured (JSON) log parser
tasks.details: Parse JSON log lines into a canonical event schema: timestamp (UTC), service, environment, severity, message, logger, request_id, trace_id, user_id (hashed), http status, latency_ms, error_code, plus a raw payload column. Handle nested fields and missing keys without throwing. Cover with fixtures from the 1.3 sample corpus.

tasks.name: 2.5 Plaintext log fallback & timestamp normalization
tasks.details: Add a regex-based fallback parser for plaintext/legacy log lines (e.g. "2026-01-02 03:04:05 ERROR [svc] msg"), normalizing mixed timezones, epoch millis, and locale date formats to UTC. Route unparseable lines to a dead-letter file with the raw line and reason. Target ≥98% parse rate on the sample corpus.

tasks.name: 2.6 Log enrichment & error classification
tasks.details: Derive analysis-ready fields: error family/category from exception class + message patterns (timeout, auth, validation, upstream 5xx, rate limit, OOM), is_error/is_warn flags, HTTP status class, latency bucket, and service tier. Maintain the taxonomy in a versioned config file; unit test each rule. Keep it rule-based — no ML in v1.

tasks.name: 2.7 Data quality checks & quarantine path
tasks.details: Define and implement blocking checks (schema match, required fields non-null, valid enum/date/status, row count within ±30% of trailing average, duplicate rate threshold) and non-blocking warnings (null spikes). Failing rows go to a quarantine table with source file, line number, and rule violated; a run summary record is written for monitoring.

tasks.name: 2.8 Orchestration & idempotent batch runs
tasks.details: Wire the CSV and log jobs into a scheduler with a clear dependency graph, retries with backoff, timeouts, and alerting on failure. Make every run idempotent via date-partition overwrite or upsert on natural keys so re-running a failed day is safe. Add a --backfill flag for historical ranges and record run metadata.

tasks.name: 3.1 Customer dimension & segment schema design
tasks.details: Design the customer dimensional model: dim_customer (SCD2 on plan/segment/status changes), dim_plan, dim_geo, and a date spine. Define surrogate keys, grain, slowly-changing behavior, and exactly which PII-masked columns are exposed. Document entity-relationship diagram and column-level definitions before writing SQL.

tasks.name: 3.2 Application-health fact table design
tasks.details: Design fct_log_event at one row per parsed log event (partitioned by date, clustered by service/severity), plus pre-aggregated fct_service_hourly (requests, errors, p95 latency, error-family counts). Choose the grain deliberately to keep dashboard queries sub-second and document cardinality estimates.

tasks.name: 3.3 Staging models & transformation project setup
tasks.details: Initialize the transformation project (dbt or SQL pipeline) with staging models (stg_customers, stg_log_events), source freshness declarations, naming conventions, and a dev/prod target split. Implement generic tests (unique, not_null, accepted_values, relationships) on staging keys. Everything must build from a clean checkout with one command.

tasks.name: 3.4 Customer lifecycle & segmentation models
tasks.details: Build mart_customer_health with one row per customer per day: tenure, plan, MRR band, activity recency, engagement score, lifecycle stage (new/active/at-risk/churned), and simple rule-based segments (high-value, dormant, new). Keep rules in a config file with owner comments so business can review thresholds.

tasks.name: 3.5 Log analysis marts (error trends & latency)
tasks.details: Build mart_service_daily and mart_error_signature_daily: requests, error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, top error signatures (normalized message), new-vs-recurring errors, and affected-customer proxy counts. Include a 7-day rolling average and day-over-day delta to support trend visuals.

tasks.name: 3.6 Partitioning, retention & cost controls
tasks.details: Apply date partitioning/clustering to fact tables, define retention (e.g. 24 months raw logs, 36 months aggregates), set up automatic archival of cold partitions, and add query guardrails (partition filters required, row limits for ad-hoc). Measure baseline table sizes and projected monthly storage/scan cost; record in a short cost memo.

tasks.name: 3.7 Data dictionary & lineage documentation
tasks.details: Auto-generate the data dictionary from model metadata (column name, type, description, owner, PII tag) and publish it to the repo docs folder. Add a lineage diagram covering source file → staging → marts → API endpoints so any metric can be traced end to end. Definition of done: a new engineer can find where any dashboard number comes from in under five minutes.

tasks.name: 4.1 Metric catalog & single definitions
tasks.details: Turn the 1.1 KPI list into a versioned metric catalog: name, plain-English definition, formula, grain, allowed dimensions, null/zero handling, owner, and source model. Resolve ambiguities (e.g. active user = login vs API call) with stakeholders in one review. Every dashboard tile must reference a metric ID from this catalog.

tasks.name: 4.2 Aggregation queries & materialized views
tasks.details: Implement one SQL/view per catalog metric family (customer KPIs, cohort retention, error rate, latency percentiles, top errors) against the M3 marts. Preview expensive rollups as materialized views refreshed on the pipeline schedule. Validate each result against a hand-calculated sample of 20 rows.

tasks.name: 4.3 API scaffolding, endpoints & OpenAPI spec
tasks.details: Stand up the API service with health check, versioned routes (/v1/metrics/{id}, /v1/customers, /v1/logs/summary), consistent pagination, filter validation, and structured error responses. Publish an OpenAPI spec and generate typed client stubs for the frontend. Include request-id logging on every call.

tasks.name: 4.4 Authentication, RBAC & row-level access
tasks.details: Add authentication (SSO or token-based), role definitions (admin, analyst, viewer), and enforce that viewer roles cannot query raw or unmasked fields. Implement row/column-level filtering per role and audit-log every metric request with user, role, and filters. Test with one user per role.

tasks.name: 4.5 Caching & query performance tuning
tasks.details: Add a cache layer for expensive metric responses keyed by metric + filters + date range, with TTL aligned to refresh cadence and explicit invalidation after pipeline runs. Profile the slowest five queries, add indexes/clustering where needed, and document measured p50/p95 before and after. Target p95 under 500 ms for dashboard calls.

tasks.name: 4.6 API contract tests & seeded fixtures
tasks.details: Create a deterministic seed dataset (customers + logs with known expected aggregates) and contract tests that fail if response shape, types, or key metric values drift. Cover filter combinations, empty results, invalid params, and unauthorized access. Run in CI on every PR.

tasks.name: 5.1 UX wireframes & dashboard layout
tasks.details: Produce low-fidelity wireframes for each page: overview, customer analytics, log/service health, and detail drilldown. Map every wireframe block to a metric ID from the catalog and note the chart type plus the question it answers. Review with 2–3 real users; capture feedback and iterate once. No code in this task.

tasks.name: 5.2 Design system, theme & chart conventions
tasks.details: Set up the frontend design foundation: color tokens (including colorblind-safe categorical palette), typography, spacing, card/panel primitives, and reusable chart wrappers with consistent axes, tooltips, legends, number formatting, and empty/loading states. Document when to use line vs bar vs area. Include a small component gallery page.

tasks.name: 5.3 App shell: routing, auth guard & data fetching
tasks.details: Build the application shell: layout with sidebar/topbar, route structure, auth guard using the M4 tokens, role-aware menu, global date-range state, and a typed API client with retry/timeout handling. Add skeleton loaders and a standard error boundary so every page degrades gracefully. Include one end-to-end smoke test.

tasks.name: 5.4 Customer analytics views
tasks.details: Implement the customer pages from the wireframes: KPI header (total/active/new/churned, MRR), segment distribution, cohort retention heatmap, lifecycle funnel, and a searchable customer table with a detail drawer. Wire to /v1 metrics endpoints, handle empty and large-result states, and match numbers to API fixtures exactly.

tasks.name: 5.5 Log analysis & service health views
tasks.details: Implement the observability pages: error-rate trend with 7-day rolling average, p95 latency chart, service health table (requests/errors/latency per service), top error signatures with volume and day-over-day change, and an error detail panel showing normalized message and first/last seen. Wire to the log summary endpoints and verify against fixtures.

tasks.name: 5.6 Global filters, drilldowns & cross-filtering
tasks.details: Add a global filter bar (date range with presets, plan, segment, service, environment, severity) persisted in the URL so views are shareable. Implement click-to-drill from chart segments into filtered tables, and make filters cross-apply across tiles on the same page. Debounce requests and show active-filter chips with a clear-all action.

tasks.name: 5.7 Export & scheduled report delivery
tasks.details: Add CSV export for tables and PNG/SVG export for charts, honoring the active filters and exposing only masked fields. Implement "schedule this view": choose frequency and recipients, render a snapshot server-side, and email a PDF link. Store schedules in a config table with owner and last-sent status. Test one schedule end to end with a fake mailer.

tasks.name: 5.8 Accessibility & responsive layout pass
tasks.details: Run an accessibility pass on all pages: keyboard navigation, visible focus, ARIA labels on charts/tables, sufficient contrast, and screen-reader-friendly table alternatives for every chart. Add responsive breakpoints so the dashboard is usable at 1280px and 768px. Fix findings and record a short audit checklist with pass/fail per page.

tasks.name: 6.1 Pipeline unit & integration test coverage
tasks.details: Define the test pyramid targets and fill gaps: unit tests for parsers, normalization rules, PII functions, and error taxonomy; integration tests that run a small CSV + log fixture through the full pipeline into marts. Assert row counts and key aggregates. Enforce a coverage floor in CI and publish the report.

tasks.name: 6.2 End-to-end regression suite for dashboard flows
tasks.details: Automate the critical user journeys with a browser test tool: log in as each role, load each page, apply a filter, drill into a chart, export CSV, and confirm numbers match the API fixtures. Run against a seeded environment in CI on a nightly schedule and on release candidates. Capture screenshots on failure.

tasks.name: 6.3 Load & performance testing
tasks.details: Script load tests for the API and key dashboard pages at expected peak (e.g. 20 concurrent users, 5x burst) using production-like data volumes, not toy fixtures. Record p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, and DB load. Identify the first bottleneck, fix it, and re-run. Publish a one-page results memo with pass/fail against the p95 target.

tasks.name: 6.4 Security review, PII & access audit
tasks.details: Run a structured review: verify no raw PII reaches marts or API responses, secrets are in a manager not the repo, dependencies are scanned for known CVEs, authz blocks viewer access to restricted fields, and audit logs capture access. Attempt 5 concrete abuse cases and record results. Obtain written security/legal sign-off.

tasks.name: 6.5 User acceptance testing & sign-off
tasks.details: Prepare a UAT script with 10–15 realistic tasks tied to the original success metrics, plus a feedback form (correctness, clarity, speed, trust in numbers). Run sessions with representative users, triage findings into must-fix vs backlog, fix must-fix items, and collect written acceptance from the business owner.

tasks.name: 6.6 Monitoring, alerting & pipeline observability
tasks.details: Instrument the pipeline and API: run success/failure, rows in/out, quarantine counts, freshness lag, API error rate and p95 latency. Create alerts for missed schedules, freshness over SLA, error-rate spikes, and quarantine above threshold, routed to the on-call channel. Build one small operational health dashboard.

tasks.name: 6.7 Runbooks, on-call guide & user documentation
tasks.details: Write runbooks for the five most likely incidents (failed nightly run, stale data, bad CSV schema, API down, slow dashboard) with symptom, diagnosis, and remediation steps. Add a user guide explaining each page, metric definitions, and refresh cadence. Record a 15-minute walkthrough video. Definition of done: someone outside the team can operate and support it.

tasks.name: 6.8 Production deployment & phased rollout
tasks.details: Provision production infrastructure as code, run the deployment checklist (backfill, smoke tests, DNS, TLS, secrets, backups), and roll out in three phases: internal team → pilot group of 5–10 users → all users. Define rollback triggers and a go/no-go checkpoint before each phase. Announce launch and collect first-week feedback.
